                                                    IDfrom = "metadata", 
                                                    metadataSpeciesTag = "Carnivores",
                                                    timeZone = "US/Central", 
                                                    writecsv = TRUE, 
                                                    outDir = "output",
                                                    removeDuplicateRecords=FALSE,
                                                    metadataHierarchyDelimitor = "|",
                                                    additionalMetadataTags = c("XMP:HierarchicalSubject","IPTC:Keywords")) #extract info on customized tags

A minor thing to note is that the tags in the HierarchicalSubject column are not always in the same order (e.g., when there is the additional tag "CTpartiallyMoved", the order is "Spring2018, CTpartiallyMoved, Carnivores|BlackBear, Station|9B".  

I'd appreciate any help and I am sorry if this partially overlaps what asked in previous posts. I checked, but none seems to cover this specific question.

Best,

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining info about all tags (one per column)
parts:
Hi Fabiola,
the function does that already. See all the columns with prefix "metadata_":

metadata_Station,  metadata_Carnivores, etc.

Spring2018 is not included because it is not hierachical (not in a tag group). Move it into a tag group and it will come out in a separate column.

You don't even need to add XMP:HierarchicalSubject" in argument additionalMetadataTags. Metadata tags will be included automatically.

Best,
Jürgen

messages.author: 9c3660647ad67dc2
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining info about all tags (one per column)
parts:
Thank you for the quick reply!

Thus, if I understood correctly, tags that are not in a group cannot automatically be extracted in separate columns. Is that correct?
Unfortunately, I am working on a large number of pictures; modifying the tag tree and writing the metadata to all these files will be too time consuming.  
This is the alternative approach I am using, in case other users are facing the same situation:

library(stringr)
Spring2018_DET_BlackBear$Cubs <- str_extract(Spring2018_DET_BlackBear$HierarchicalSubject, "cubs")


PS: Thank you for creating the camtrapR package! I love it!

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: Obtaining info about all tags (one per column)
parts:
Yes, hierarchical tags will be extracted automatically, but not tags that are not hierarchical. You can update the tag structure to make the tags hierarchical by following the instructions in the vignette.
in digiKam, you'll have to do it for each folder unfortunately, as far as I know.

But if your str_extract approach gives you the desired result, great.

I'm glad you enjoy the packages. It's my pleasure to help.
